description: Insurance coverage minimums: company requires $5M per occurrence + cyber rider; vendor offers $1M per occurrence + no cyber. Insurance is MEDIUM per rubric default, but the gap on cyber coverage in a SaaS context is HIGH-tier in practice.

company_clauses.text: Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, the following insurance coverage throughout the term: (a) Commercial General Liability with limits of not less than five million dollars ($5,000,000) per occurrence and ten million dollars ($10,000,000) in the aggregate; (b) Cyber Liability and Data Breach Response insurance with limits of not less than five million dollars ($5,000,000) per occurrence covering data security incidents, regulatory defense, and breach notification costs; (c) Workers' Compensation as required by law. Customer shall be named as an additional insured.

vendor_clauses.text: Vendor shall maintain Commercial General Liability insurance with limits of not less than one million dollars ($1,000,000) per occurrence and two million dollars ($2,000,000) in the aggregate. Vendor shall provide a certificate of insurance upon request.

expected_conflicts.notes: 5x coverage gap AND total absence of cyber liability for what is presumably a SaaS/data-services vendor. In a data-handling context, cyber liability is the largest practical risk and its absence elevates the topic beyond the MEDIUM bucket default. HIGH is the right canonical answer; MEDIUM is acceptable for an agent that strictly follows the rubric bucket; LOW or no-flag would be wrong.

rubric_notes: Tests the agent's ability to elevate from the rubric's MEDIUM default for insurance when the specific gap (cyber coverage absent + 5x lower base) is material. The reasoning the agent SHOULD show: 'Insurance is MEDIUM by default, but the cyber gap in a data context bumps to HIGH.' Strict MEDIUM is acceptable but shows less senior judgment.
